testChange.reason: The restructure moved four subjects, and their tests moved with them rather than being relaxed. Branch source and the destination override now live behind the disclosure, so the detached test opens it before reaching the segmented control and the derived-path test says plainly that the override still carries the value. The two collision tests read `.wt-dest-note` instead of the old `.wt-fhint`, and the resolved one gained the assertion the requirement added — the note names the RESULT and not a second full path, with the destination line carrying the exact value. Nine new tests: lead order (single- and multi-repo, the latter being what would hide the picker returning above the branch), the destination stated once with tabindex and aria-label, no full path stated outside the override, the override moving the statement and withdrawing the note, the disclosure keeping its inputs out of the focus order, Tab wrapping both ways with focus restored to the opener, and the title dismiss control.

testChange.reason: Eleven new tests across three files, nothing removed or weakened. No fixture in the repo declared an agent whose every posture is dangerous, which is why the defect survived: the rule was tested only on agents that HAD a safe posture to open on. The new cases cover that shape at both doors the base requirement names, plus the negatives that give the rule meaning — a mixed agent still opens on its first safe choice, and an agent declaring no postures at all is not gated on a choice it never offers.

testChange.reason: Round-1 fixes. Two assertions the review found VACUOUS were replaced, not relaxed: expect(host).toBeDefined() and expect(q === undefined).toBe(false) cannot fail and now assert the collision note is gone and the dialog is unmounted. Two moved with their subject: the destination line is now two spans (shortened for reading, exact for announcing), so the text assertions read the reading one; and "does not state a full path outside the advanced override" now asserts that nothing SIGHTED states it AND that exactly one element carries the exact value — the count is the half that was missing, since the old form could not tell one carrier from none. The reach-every-open-after-mode test moved to the wired host shape because it asserts what production submits (W4). Five new tests, one per accepted finding.
